catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds a persistent ROS geometry_msgs/Twist velocity publication for a world.sim. cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 requires a bounded duration and returns distance, heading and a stopped state that the upstream /cmd_vel publisher cannot acknowledge; cap.motion.cartesian_twist.v1 requires a duration and binds robot.arm. The extension preserves the native topic and reports publication evidence only.
catalogue_requests.summary: Publish one geometry_msgs/Twist velocity setpoint on the upstream /cmd_vel topic.

BLOCKED (HELPER_MISSING): the pinned package is a Gazebo simulation with a Pioneer 3DX mobile base, but its only in-package command endpoint is the teleop's relative cmd_vel publication, and the clone registers no acknowledged stop service or action. The teleop advertises geometry_msgs::Twist on "cmd_vel" (src/key_control.cpp:178) and the robot model configures the Gazebo differential-drive plugin to subscribe to commandTopic cmd_vel (urdf/pioneer3dx_body.xacro:331). The package builds exactly one executable, key_control, from src/key_control.cpp (CMakeLists.txt:30-31). The q key returns without publishing a zero (src/key_control.cpp:256-259). The stock RosDriver cannot prove an acknowledged stop from a zero-velocity topic publication, and the SDK states that a zero-velocity publication is not an acknowledged stop (MHS/sdk/docs/ros-driver.md). The declaration therefore preserves the primary velocity command but leaves safety_bindings empty and claims no safe state. G8 fail with G8.CONFORMANCE MHS-Sim CL3 not achieved (level CL1), failing TCAP-003 and SAFE-028: the command has no observable device effect beyond transmission and no acknowledged safe state exists. G9 skip (G9.NOT_RUN). The failed list in check-report.json is [G6, G8]. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings were reported. MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block: the pinned catkin package builds one executable, the keyboard teleop key_control (CMakeLists.txt:30-31), whose only output is a relative cmd_vel Twist (key_control.cpp:178), and the Pioneer 3DX gazebo_ros_diff_drive plugin subscribes to commandTopic cmd_vel under robotNamespace / (pioneer3dx_body.xacro:320-341); no service or action in the clone can acknowledge a stop and a zero-velocity publication is transmission-only, so the stock e-stop fails G6.ESTOP_FAILED with the latch held and G8 fails SAFE-028 and TCAP-003. The endpoint, the Twist type, the facts, the operator_required linear and angular inputs and the R2 raise for a mobile base on the generic /cmd_vel were checked and are right. The reviewer changed no authored file; the gate re-run rewrote check-report.json with the same findings. For the next author: the shipped launch also starts move_base at the root namespace without a remap (warehouse_simulation.launch:44-60), and stock move_base publishes cmd_vel relative to its namespace (outside the clone), so it is a second commander on the same /cmd_vel once RViz or another client sends a goal, which the package does not disclose; the first fact's 'so ... rather than a hardware node' clause is an inference beyond its lines; and the diff-drive plugin's units are outside the clone, so the inputs rightly stay unit 1. For the human reviewer: Simulation only (ROS 1 Gazebo warehouse world with a Pioneer 3DX). The bound /cmd_vel is the generic root topic that many real mobile bases also subscribe to, so pointing this driver at a real robot's rosbridge would drive it, which is why the package stays R2. The shipped warehouse_simulation.launch also starts move_base (a second /cmd_vel commander), gmapping and RViz. Unblocking needs an acknowledged stop, for example a Gazebo pause or world-control service bound with honest pause semantics, or an SDK profile that accepts a zero-velocity command plus a sensed standstill on /odom.
